extracted.intended_audience: internet readers who enjoy satire/meme culture and reductress-style humor
extracted.subtask_description: Creating short, satirical headlines in the Reductress vein: deadpan, brand-aware, feminist-leaning parody lines that are highly sharable and work as standalone jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Say the quiet part with a straight face
rubrics_metrics.description: Satire works best when the headline says the quiet part with a straight face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver blunt or taboo observations deadpan rather than overtly winking; the humor comes from presenting the uncomfortable truth as if it's ordinary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nail the modern tone (self-help/brand voice)
rubrics_metrics.description: They nail the modern tone, the self help that sells candles, the empowerment that sends a newsletter, the product launch that solves a problem you never had.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mimic contemporary marketing/self-help/newsletter language and cadence so the headline reads like a real piece of lifestyle copy being gently mocked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration: specific enough to sting, broad enough to stick
rubrics_metrics.description: The fun is in the calibration, just specific enough to sting, just broad enough to stick to your own week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a balance where details are specific enough to provoke recognition and discomfort, but general enough that many readers can see themselves in it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersect lifestyle advice with rage shopping
rubrics_metrics.description: These gems live where lifestyle advice intersects with rage shopping, where a paragraph can feel like a mirror held at a flattering distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine the tone of prescriptive lifestyle content with consumerist anger or desire to create a sharp, relatable juxtaposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflective resonance — a flattering mirror
rubrics_metrics.description: A paragraph can feel like a mirror held at a flattering distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write lines that let readers recognize themselves (or their impulses) while still softening the blow so the joke feels affectionate rather than purely mean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gently roasted tone
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have ever laughed and then felt gently roasted by a sentence, you know the vibe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target the reader’s foibles with mild, witty mockery rather than vicious attacks; the best lines sting and comfort simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose 'soft lies' and hidden marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect satire memes that sharpen soft lies... The best ones reveal the copy underneath the copy, the sales pitch hiding in the self care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use headlines to unmask cultural clichés and marketing euphemisms—point out what branding or wellness language is actually selling or concealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feminist side-eye at wellness/branding
rubrics_metrics.description: Feminist memes that side eye the wellness machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a perspective that questions or critiques gendered consumer culture and wellness industry tropes; feminist critique is a common ideological lens here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody that clarifies chaos
rubrics_metrics.description: Parody memes that translate chaos into clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parody to reorder or name everyday absurdities so the joke makes the underlying ridiculousness feel obvious and comprehensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standalone clarity — headline works without clicking
rubrics_metrics.description: There are headlines that belong on tote bags, articles you can hear without clicking, and winks for anyone who has ever rolled their eyes at a brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write headlines that convey the joke and context by themselves; the headline should often be sufficient to land the humor without needing the article body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity with impact — 'tiny essays with chores'
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines are tiny essays with chores, which is why satire memes, feminist memes, and parody memes travel, they are digestible and devastating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep copy short and portable while packing a layered insight or emotional hit; concise phrasing increases shareability and punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merchability / cultural stickiness
rubrics_metrics.description: There are headlines that belong on tote bags...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for lines that are catchy and memorable enough to be repeated, shared, or turned into merch—phrases that stick in cultural circulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shareability and audience targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Send a favorite to the friend who owns three planners and the coworker who speaks fluent newsletter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft headlines that different audience segments can immediately recognize and forward to one another; nods to specific subcultures (e.g., planner-obsessed, newsletter devotees) increase viral potential.
